entities.summary:
Polemon I Pythodoros was the Roman Client King of Cilicia, Pontus, Colchis, and the Bosporan Kingdom, ruling from 74 BCE until his death in 7 BCE. As the son and heir of Zenon, he may have also been the son of Tryphaena.

Polemon was a key figure in the Hellenistic world, playing a significant role in the politics and culture of the region. He was known for his diplomatic skills and his ability to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the various Hellenistic kingdoms.

Despite his importance, Polemon's legacy is not as well-documented as some other figures of the time. However, his reign marked an important period in the history of the region, as the Roman Client Kingdoms began to consolidate their power and influence.

The significance of Polemon's reign can be seen in the fact that he was one of the last Roman Client Kings to rule over the region. His death in 7 BCE marked the end of an era and the beginning of a new period of Roman expansion and dominance.

Polemon's contribution to the cultural heritage of the region cannot be overstated. He was a patron of the arts and a supporter of education, and his reign saw the establishment of several important cultural institutions.

The impact of Polemon's reign can still be felt today, with many of the cultural and historical institutions he established still existing in some form.
